UnitStatement: This file defines the initial maintainer policy skeleton for OpenPipeStress.
The MAINTAINERS file is a governance artifact, not a legal opinion, professional engineering approval, certification, sealing, or code-compliance claim.
The draft maintainer policy is aligned to execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7 and approved DAG-006 coordination authority.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md and DAG-006 define current package and deliverable scope and active dependency relationships.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7 and DAG-006 do not by themselves approve releases, lifecycle transitions, professional reliance, code-compliance claims, or final governance decisions.
Project intent is a source-available noncommercial piping stress analysis platform.
Decomposition authority is execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7.
Coordination graph authority is the execution/_DAG/DAG-006/ active edge set; candidate rows remain non-gating.
The project license is PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0, documented in LICENSE.md and at polyformproject.org/licenses/noncommercial/1.0.0.
The interim contributor certification mechanism is the template in governance/CONTRIBUTOR_CERTIFICATION_TEMPLATE.md; the final DCO/CLA/other mechanism remains TBD.
The maintainer roster is TBD.
Release authority is TBD.
Legal-review authority is TBD.

Human project authority record is TBD.
No contributor, maintainer, agent, or release note may state a final governance authority until the corresponding TBD is resolved by the human project authority.
The project license has been selected by human project authority as PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0.
Maintainers are responsible for project stewardship within the boundaries in docs/CONTRACT.md, docs/DIRECTIVE.md, docs/IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md, and docs/VALIDATION_STRATEGY.md.
Maintainers must preserve stable package, deliverable, scope, objective, decision, issue, and risk IDs.
Maintainers must use the current decomposition, approved DAG, and deliverable-local lifecycle files as coordination evidence without treating them as release acceptance.
Maintainers must enforce the open-mechanics/private-code-data boundary.
Maintainers must require source, provenance, license or redistribution status, contributor certification, and review disposition for public data contributions.
Maintainers must quarantine suspected protected standards content, proprietary data, or private project data before merge or release.
Maintainers must keep missing engineering, legal, governance, or release choices as TBD, except for the selected project license.
Maintainers must require tests, validation evidence, or explicit deferrals appropriate to the changed surface.
Maintainers must prevent product claims that imply certification, endorsement, sealing, authentication, or automatic code compliance.
Maintainers must record accepted governance decisions in public artifacts or decision records.
Every public contribution must pass the defined review gates before merge or have an explicit recorded maintainer deferral.
Scope-and-identity gate: the change must map to an accepted deliverable, issue, or maintainer-approved maintenance task.

IP-and-provenance gate: the contribution must contain no protected standards text, copied standards tables, proprietary vendor data, private rule packs, or private project data without documented redistribution rights.
Data-boundary gate: public examples must use invented, original, public-domain, or permissively licensed data only.
Tests-and-evidence gate: required tests, validation checks, documentation updates, or explicit deferrals must be present.
Product-claims gate: user-facing text must not claim certification, approval, endorsement, sealing, or code compliance for reliance.
Privacy gate: telemetry, bug reports, examples, and exports must not include private engineering data by default.
Public data contributions must also record specified evidence slots before acceptance.
Source-identity evidence slot requires source name and source location, or TBD if the source is still under review.
Redistribution-basis evidence slot requires license or redistribution status, including whether the data is public, private-only, unknown, or suspected protected content.
Contributor-certification evidence slot requires a contributor statement that the data is original, invented, public-domain, permissively licensed, or otherwise redistributable.
Review-disposition evidence slot must be pending, accepted, rejected, quarantined, or TBD with a reason.
Quarantine-status evidence slot is required when protected standards content, proprietary data, or private project data is suspected.
Private-data-risk evidence slot requires a review note confirming whether the contribution can expose private project, rule-pack, material, component, owner-standard, or company design-basis data.
The default contributor certification record is governance/CONTRIBUTOR_CERTIFICATION_TEMPLATE.md.
The default review record for the contribution review gates is governance/CONTRIBUTION_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md.
A maintainer may use a project issue, pull-request template, or release checklist instead only when it preserves the same evidence fields and disposition states.
A public release must not be published until maintainers complete a release review covering the specified items.
Release review must cover an explicit human release decision and a recorded governance authority basis.
Release review must cover release scope, changed surfaces, and any excluded or deferred work.
Release review must cover selected license and notices, including PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 and the corresponding LICENSE.md notice.
Release review must cover validation status and known limitations.
Release review must cover data-boundary constraints and professional-responsibility notices.
Release review must cover protected-content and provenance review for public examples, templates, and bundled data.
Release review must cover private-data and telemetry review.
Release review must cover reproducibility evidence such as version, commit, build, schema, model, and rule-pack checksum behavior where applicable.
Release review must cover human review of release notes and product claims.
Release maturity labels remain TBD.
No release label may imply professional reliance, code compliance, certification, endorsement, or engineering approval.

Governance decisions affecting license, contributor certification, maintainer authority, release criteria, public-data acceptance, professional-responsibility language, security reporting, or private-data handling must be recorded.

A recorded governance decision must include decision ID, date, decision status, decision owner or human authority, affected documents or packages, rationale and source references, and reconsideration trigger.
The ADR location and numbering convention remain TBD.

GOV-TBD-005 (what security disclosure channel and response process will be used) is TBD.

GOV-TBD-007 (who has legal-review authority for protected-content, contributor, release, and license questions) is TBD.
GOV-TBD-008 (what release-label vocabulary and human-acceptance workflow will be used without implying professional approval or code compliance) is TBD.
Maintainers must pause review and escalate when a contribution may contain protected standards text, tables, figures, examples, copied formulas, or proprietary data.
Maintainers must pause review and escalate when a contribution lacks source, provenance, license or redistribution status, or contributor certification.
Maintainers must pause review and escalate when a user-facing claim could be read as certification, endorsement, sealing, authentication, or professional code-compliance approval.
Maintainers must pause review and escalate when a proposed public release has unresolved protected-content, private-data, validation, or product-claim issues.
Maintainers must pause review and escalate when a governance decision would resolve a TBD without a recorded human ruling.
